clue.text: Rupees stored to send overseas?

parts.note: R, the abbreviation for rupees, kept in a depot or store reads ..., so the two words describe the answer's letters

explanation.surface: Money kept back in reserve, ready to be shipped abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stored' implies DEPOT, a storehouse, and also says R goes into it, so the wordplay is read as a picture of what the answer looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: To deport someone is to expel them from a country, usually shipping them abroad.

clue.text: Cancer, perhaps, in ruminant — one creating something new?

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a deer chews the cud, so it is a ruminant
Cancer is one sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A zodiac crab sits inside a cud-chewing animal, then a question about an inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who creates new clothes, products or layouts is called by the job title for an originator of patterns.

clue.text: Range of colourants allowed in meat paste

indicators.note: in places the allowed word inside the meat paste

parts.note: pâté is a meat paste
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Food colouring permitted in a savoury spread.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's board holds a range of paints, and the word extends to any chosen set of colours.

clue.text: Scent went up with rate changing

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, went up

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of rate are rearranged

explanation.surface: A perfume's price climbed as the rate shifted.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fragrant liquid made from distilled petals, used as a perfume and flavouring.

clue.text: Tropical tree monkey died

parts.note: a tamarin is a small South American monkey
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A monkey has died in a tropical tree.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an African tree grown throughout the tropics for its sour pods.

clue.text: One making a defence about name through expert in human affairs

indicators.note: about means going round, so the defender wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: an apologist argues in defence of a cause
thro is an old shortened spelling of through

explanation.surface: A defender wraps a name inside himself on the way to becoming a student of people.
explanation.definitionFit: This scientist studies human societies, cultures and their development.

clue.text: A lot of what might be ginger jelly

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: ginger is an example of a spice

explanation.surface: A wobbly dessert flavoured mostly with ginger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is taken as written; 'lot of' cuts the final E from SPICE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a savoury jelly made with meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: One problem's arisen about favourite drive

parts.note: one is the roman numeral I

indicators.note: about means the turned-round sum goes around the favourite
in a down clue, arisen means the word for problem is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A single difficulty has come up concerning a favourite motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arisen' turns SUM into MUS; ''s' is just 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive in the sense of motivation or momentum is a synonym of this force pushing something on.

clue.text: Departs from the city, one in South Africa

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
urban means belonging to a city

explanation.surface: Someone leaves town, heading for a place in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: This port on the Indian Ocean coast is a large city in South Africa, the 'one' the clue points to.

clue.text: Copy charladies frantic for carbohydrate

indicators.note: frantic means wildly disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Cleaners in a frenzy copying something about sugars.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch and cellulose are examples of this kind of carbohydrate, built from many sugar units.

clue.text: Talk about pound and spend freely

indicators.note: about says the talk word goes round the pounding word

parts.note: to spout is to talk at length
to lash is to beat or pound

explanation.surface: Chat about sterling and lavish spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money next to 'spend' but is the verb, to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to spend lavishly on something, an idiom for being extravagant.

clue.text: Musician with piano appearing in seaside attraction

indicators.note: appearing in says one piece shows up inside the other

parts.note: a pier is a classic British seaside attraction, a walkway with amusements built out over the sea
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A pianist plays at the end of the pier.
explanation.definitionFit: This musician plays the bagpipes or another pipe instrument.

clue.text: Flight having time due to arrive back for point of entry

indicators.note: having says the flight word keeps the arrival time but in altered form

parts.note: a getaway is an escape, a flight

indicators.note: back says the arrival time is read in reverse

parts.note: ETA is estimated time of arrival

explanation.surface: A flight's arrival is running late, ahead of boarding.
explanation.walkthrough: The ETA within the escape word is turned round by 'back', giving ATE in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an opening or arch through which one enters, a way in.

clue.text: Girl eating a little cottage cheese

indicators.note: eating says the girl's name takes in the other piece

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name
cot is an old word for a small cottage

explanation.surface: A girl tucking into a small amount of cottage cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cottage cheese' looks like the definition; 'cheese' alone is.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a soft Italian whey cheese.

clue.text: Up before court

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Rise before appearing at court.
explanation.definitionFit: Up in the sense of upright or standing is a synonym of this adjective.

clue.text: Piece of software has put up price

parts.note: an app is a piece of software
to raise is to put up

explanation.surface: A new app has caused a price increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'price' looks like a noun but is the verb, to put a value on.
explanation.definitionFit: To price something in the sense of valuing it is to assess its worth, a synonym.

clue.text: Job in space needs a mostly robust adult regularly employed

indicators.note: mostly says all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: strong means robust

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A space mission requires a sturdy grown-up in steady work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts STRONG to STRON; 'regularly' takes AUT from 'adult'. The definition is loose: it names the person by the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose job takes them into space is a space traveller, a cosmonaut by another name.

clue.text: Concern mounting in support of mountain region for wine

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece in support of another sits below it

parts.note: berg means mountain, as in iceberg and German

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means climbing, so the concern word is read upwards

parts.note: care means concern

explanation.surface: Worry grows about supporting a mountain district known for its wine.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a wine-producing area in south-west France, near Bordeaux.

clue.text: Marks article unusually showing poetic quality

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of article come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece by Marks is remarkably poetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse showing a regular rhythm or measure is described with this adjective about metre.

clue.text: Gloss ruined axle pin

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A damaged axle pin needs some account given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gloss' looks like a noun (shine) but is the verb, to give a commentary.
explanation.definitionFit: To gloss a text is to add notes that interpret it, the same as making it clear.

clue.text: Goddess needing something of a reality check

indicators.note: something of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deity needs to come down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'needing', but that is the link word joining definition to wordplay; 'Goddess' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Greek goddess of fortune and chance.

clue.text: Rest times following being unwell during tea

indicators.note: following says the times sign comes after the rest
during says the unwell piece is set within the tea

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
ill means unwell
X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: Taking it easy after falling ill over tea.
explanation.definitionFit: This slang verb, a blend of chill and relax, means to rest or calm down.

clue.text: Turning over, leave out a page all the way through

indicators.note: turning over says the whole string is read the other way

parts.note: to miss is to leave out

explanation.surface: Flipping pages and skipping one while reading right through.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin word used in footnotes means throughout a text, found in many places.

clue.text: Old jar of what could be insect repellent — unopened, note

indicators.note: unopened means without its first letter

parts.note: camphor is used as a moth repellent
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: An ancient jar of bug spray left sealed, with a message attached.
explanation.definitionFit: This two-handled vessel was used in ancient Greece and Rome for wine and oil.

clue.text: Mature way of working upset Greek character

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: to age is to mature
MO is modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: An older Greek's habits have been disrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Grand sound of cows looking extremely healthy

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
lowing is the mooing of cattle

explanation.surface: A splendid mooing from cattle in fine fettle.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing complexion is rosy and radiant, a sign of good health.

clue.text: Fish consumed after missing meal of steak?

indicators.note: after says the consumed word follows what remains
missing says the meal's letters are taken out of steak

parts.note: tea is a meal, in Britain an early evening one
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Fish eaten instead of a steak dinner?
explanation.walkthrough: STEAK less TEA leaves SK. The question mark nods to the answer being an anagram of steak, though that is not the mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat cartilaginous fish is related to the rays.

clue.text: One moving into a new position inches higher

definitions.text: One moving into a new position

parts.note: INS is the abbreviation for inches
taller means higher

explanation.surface: Someone shifting to a fresh spot gains a few inches.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who installs another in office or fits equipment puts it in a new position.

clue.text: What could be lion trapping an ox, perhaps, in endless plain

indicators.note: trapping says the shortened plain word holds the other pieces
endless says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: mere means plain or simple
an is the indefinite article, here A
neat is an old word for cattle, of which an ox is one

explanation.surface: A lion catching an ox somewhere on an endless plain.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAT is an old word for cattle, and 'plain' is the adjective (mere, simple), not grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion that attacks people is an example of this kind of predator, so the definition gives an instance.

clue.text: A cab caught having lost control of motion

parts.note: a taxi is a cab
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cabbie is caught after losing control of the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical adjective describes a person unable to coordinate their muscle movements.
